correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the conditional G(n-r,m) law after prescribing an ordered r-tuple of isolated vertices, the exact tree-copy factorial expectation, and the cancellation of m and tree automorphisms. Verified the adjacent ratio and its strictly decreasing linear sign numerator algebraically; exact R(2)=1 and strict R(3)>1 imply at most one subsequent level-one crossing. The uniform logarithmic expansion gives g(x)=log(1-x)+2x and a nondegenerate positive root; its O(n^-1) correction yields the precise interpolated crossing. The standalone graph enumeration and algebraic tester passed 39,788 checks including all 33,856 labeled graphs on four to six vertices. Computation is supplemental; domain excludes inadmissible m, induced tree counts, and r varying with n for the asymptotic.

originality.rationale: The elementary inclusion probability is acknowledged as classical. Inspected full text of Janson–Ruciński (2009) and accessible abstracts of Janson (1990) and Tomescu (1994); none of the inspected statements implies the joint finite, shape/edge-budget-independent sign profile for macroscopic trees. Targeted mathematical-alias and implication searches did not expose a dominating published formula. Full access to two relevant historical primary papers was unavailable, so priority is best-knowledge rather than definitive.
residual_risks: The primary full text of Janson (1990) was inaccessible; its abstract describes fixed-motif functional asymptotics, but the paper may contain more general formulas.
The primary full text of Tomescu (1994) was inaccessible; its abstract describes overlap among macroscopic subtrees, not the joint covariance here.
A standard but less readily searchable general factorial-moment theorem might subsume the exact finite ratio; searches cannot establish absolute priority.

value.rationale: The complete dependence classification answers a natural question about the effect of conditioning on total edges: independent-edge graphs have negative isolate/tree covariance, but fixed-edge graphs have a positive phase and a universal sign reversal at the nontrivial fraction rho≈0.796812. The result is valid for every tree shape, all admissible edge budgets, and every fixed factorial order; the exact finite single-crossing property and order-one threshold correction explain the boundary, beyond an arbitrary parameter substitution or a standalone known expectation.
